transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hello, doctor. Thank you. Well, I came because... it’s getting to be a bit much, really. I spend far too much of my day opening the same folders, and drawers, and my labeled boxes, again and again. Just to make sure the important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. 

Which is silly, I know, but... oh, speaking of keepsakes, I have this lovely silver locket in one of the drawers. My husband gave it to me right after I finished my bachelor's degree. We took a train up to the mountains that very weekend to celebrate. The leaves were just beautiful that time of year, all reds and golds, and we stayed at this little inn that smelled like pine needles and fresh biscuits. I haven't had a biscuit like that since... 

But, oh, I'm sorry, where was I? Yes, the boxes and the papers. I just keep checking them. Even when I just checked a few minutes before and I know I just looked, I find myself walking right back over to open them up all over again.
Do you feel anxious or upset if you try to stop yourself from checking the folders and boxes?

Oh, terribly upset. It’s... well, even when I know better, a thought will just keep needling me. I'll start thinking that maybe I threw away my husband's old tax papers by mistake, or that I accidentally put a family recipe in the wrong box. 

And oh, those recipes are so precious. There's one for a peach cobbler that my mother used to make every August. We had this magnificent peach tree in our backyard when I was a little girl. The neighborhood boys would always try to hop the fence to steal them, but our dog, Buster—he was a golden retriever, such a sweet boy but very protective of that yard—would bark and chase them right back over the fence. I think I still have Buster's old collar in one of the memory boxes... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, stopping myself from checking. Yes, if I try to ignore the thought, I just can't seem to let it pass. I start feeling like I've done something terribly careless, and the only way to fix that awful feeling is to go and look.
